# Overview

Most CPTAC data come from cohorts with their own patients rather than TCGA
tumors: the CPTAC-3 discovery and confirmatory cohorts (e.g. clear cell
renal cell carcinoma, glioblastoma, lung adenocarcinoma) and the CPTAC-2
Prospective collections. Each cohort is profiled in several Proteomic Data
Commons (PDC) studies, one for each experiment, such as the proteome and the
phosphoproteome. `getCPTAC()` downloads the studies of a cohort and combines
them in one `MultiAssayExperiment`, with the PDC clinical data of the
patients as `colData`.

To add CPTAC data run on TCGA tumors to a `MultiAssayExperiment` from
`curatedTCGAData`, use `appendCPTAC()` instead; see the vignette "Adding
CPTAC proteomics to a TCGA MultiAssayExperiment"
(`vignette("CPTACdata", package = "CPTACdata")`).

```{r load-packages, message = FALSE}
library(CPTACdata)
library(MultiAssayExperiment)
```

# Which cohorts are available?

`cptacCohorts` has one row per PDC study. Its columns are:

- `cohort`: the cohort the study belongs to.
- `experiment`: the name of the experiment in the `MultiAssayExperiment`.
- `pdc_study_id`: the PDC study identifier.
- `pdc_name`: the PDC study name.
- `pdc_project`: the PDC project, "CPTAC3 Discovery and Confirmatory" or
    "CPTAC-2".
- `analytical_fraction`: the PDC analytical fraction, such as Proteome,
    Phosphoproteome or Acetylome.
- `experiment_type`: the labeling or acquisition, such as `TMT10` or
    `Label Free`.
- `data_type`: the PDC quantification matrix that is downloaded, or `NA`.

`cptacCohorts` ships with the package and needs no network access:

```{r list-cptac-cohorts}
data("cptacCohorts", package = "CPTACdata")
table(cptacCohorts[["cohort"]])
cptacCohorts[
    cptacCohorts[["cohort"]] == "CPTAC CCRCC Discovery Study",
    c("experiment", "pdc_study_id", "analytical_fraction", "data_type")
]
```

Some studies, such as most metabolome and lipidome studies, have
`data_type = NA`. The PDC holds their biospecimen records, but its API
returns no quantification matrix, so `getCPTAC()` skips them.

# Downloading a cohort

The dry run and the download query the PDC API at
`https://pdc.cancer.gov/graphql`. Biospecimen and clinical tables are cached
for the R session, so a dry run followed by a download fetches each one only
once.

The CPTAC data are provided under the PDC Data Use Agreement at
<https://proteomic.datacommons.cancer.gov/pdc/data-use-guidelines>. Read it
before running the next chunk, which accepts it on your behalf for this
document:

```{r accept-pdc-dua}
options(CPTACdata.acceptDUA = TRUE)
```

A dry run shows, for each study, whether it has a matrix and how many
patients and aliquots it covers, without downloading any matrix:

```{r cohort-dry-run}
getCPTAC("CPTAC CCRCC Discovery Study", dry_run = TRUE)
```

By default `getCPTAC()` downloads every study of the cohort that has a
matrix. Use `experiments` to choose some of them. Here we download the
proteome only:

```{r get-cohort, message = FALSE}
ccrcc <- getCPTAC("CPTAC CCRCC Discovery Study", experiments = "Proteome")
ccrcc
```

# What the object contains

Each experiment is a `SummarizedExperiment` with one assay, named after its
`data_type`. For TMT studies this is `log2_ratio`: the log2 ratio of a
sample's abundance to the common reference the PDC used for the whole study.
Label-free studies have `precursor_area` instead, which is not on a log
scale.

Columns keep the labels of the PDC matrix, which for these cohorts are the
PDC aliquot identifiers. Technical replicates keep the `.1`, `.2` suffix the
PDC gives them; use `replicates = "first"` to keep only the first replicate
of each sample. Reference channels, such as the internal reference pool, QC
samples and NCI-7 cell lines, are dropped.

The `colData` of each experiment describes its samples:

```{r cohort-samples}
colData(ccrcc[["Proteome"]])
table(ccrcc[["Proteome"]][["sample_type"]])
```

The `sampleMap` links each column to its patient, so a patient's tumor and
normal samples share one row of the `colData` of the
`MultiAssayExperiment`. That `colData` holds the PDC clinical data, with
values kept as the PDC reports them:

```{r cohort-clinical}
head(colData(ccrcc)[, c("gender", "primary_diagnosis", "tumor_grade")])
```

Each experiment also records where its data came from, including the PDC
study version and the time the matrix was downloaded:

```{r cohort-metadata}
S4Vectors::metadata(ccrcc[["Proteome"]])
```
